clue.text: Weapon much used by a knight

parts.note: a lance is a long weapon carried by a mounted knight
a lot means a great deal, much

explanation.surface: A knight's favourite weapon gets plenty of use in the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the lance the knight's weapon; in fact the knight is the definition, Arthur's most famous champion, and the weapon is only the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the best-known knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Devastator left Scout movement

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters of the word scout being moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Boy Scout walks out of the Scout movement and wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout movement' reads as Baden-Powell's youth organisation, but 'movement' is the anagram signal on the word Scout alone, placed after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of locusts strip crops bare, so the insect is a classic destroyer of harvests.

clue.text: Jab that's largely unnecessary

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, with its final letters cut away

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

explanation.surface: An injection that is mostly pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' drops the last two letters, SS, from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A jab is British slang for an injection, given with a hypodermic needle; the instrument stands for the shot.

clue.text: The old girl enters and turns over without difficulty

indicators.note: turns over in a down clue means the whole assembled piece is read from the bottom upwards
enters means the girl's name goes inside the old form of the

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
Lisa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An elderly woman comes in and rolls over effortlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old girl' looks like one phrase for an elderly woman, but it splits into two pieces; 'enters' puts the girl inside, giving YLISAE, and 'turns over' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something easily means doing it with no trouble, so the adverb matches the phrase.

clue.text: Extra item on bill — not the first to fleece

indicators.note: not the first tells us to remove the opening letter of the phrase

parts.note: a cover charge is an extra sum added to a restaurant bill

explanation.surface: A restaurant adds a surcharge to the bill to rip off its diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first' drops the C from COVER CHARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them, and charging them too much is one way to do it.

clue.text: Loss of will makes girl lose head with Jack

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and AB, able seaman, is a sailor too

indicators.note: lose head means the girl's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Julia is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl who has lost her head over a lad called Jack can no longer make decisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose head' takes the J from JULIA, leaving ULIA. AB goes first even though Jack comes last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Abulia is a medical term for a lack of willpower or inability to make decisions.

clue.text: Figaro, say, on lines of a thorny item

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Figaro is the barber of Seville in Rossini's opera, so he is an example of a barber
RY, railway, means lines of track

explanation.surface: Figaro the opera barber sings about a prickly object.
explanation.definitionFit: Barberry is a spiny shrub, a thorny plant with sharp spines along its stems.

clue.text: Bird on country track

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: land means a country, as in a foreign land
a rail is the metal track a train runs on

explanation.surface: A bird stands on a country track.
explanation.definitionFit: The landrail is another name for the corncrake, a bird of the rail family.

clue.text: Let haste be their work!

indicators.note: be their work suggests the words let haste being worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A motto for runners: hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LET HASTE is the answer, and the whole clue also describes runners, for whom speed is the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes such as sprinters are people whose task is to be fast, so haste is their work.

clue.text: 157½o in a box of games equipment

indicators.note: in means the bearing letters go inside the box word

parts.note: a chest is a box
a compass bearing of 157½ degrees is south-south-east, SSE

explanation.surface: Something set at an odd angle inside a box of games kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are 22½ degrees apart, so 157½ degrees from north is the seventh point round, south-south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess set, board and pieces, is equipment for a game.

clue.text: Roger in maid's clutches is a tool

indicators.note: the maid's clutches hold the R, putting it inside her

parts.note: a wench is an old word for a maid or serving girl
Roger stands for R in the radio alphabet, meaning received

explanation.surface: A man called Roger in a servant's embrace is a lout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a man's name; in radio talk it means R. The British slang sense of 'tool' (a fool) adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a tool for gripping and turning nuts and bolts.

clue.text: Useful adjunct for tongue of beef

definitions.text: Useful adjunct for tongue of beef

parts.words: Useful adjunct for tongue of beef
parts.note: reads like a seasoning for ox tongue on a plate, but means a block that cattle lick for minerals

explanation.definitionFit: A salt lick is a mineral block put out for cattle to lick, so it serves the tongues of beef animals.

clue.text: King, first of 18

definitions.meaning: six British kings have carried this name
the first name of the man in 18, the American writer, named after the first US President

explanation.walkthrough: 18 is WASHINGTON IRVING; George Washington's first name is GEORGE, and the writer was named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: George is a royal name and also the first name of 18 across, the writer Washington Irving's namesake.

clue.text: Pervading feeling of hope master produces

indicators.note: produces suggests the letters of hope master being made into something new

explanation.surface: A teacher's optimism creates a mood in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place is the mood or feeling that spreads through it.

clue.text: Brute gains device for achieving power

annotationWithheld.why: Brute gains device for achieving power (3,7): an anagram of BRUTE GAINS, but no word signals it except 'device', which is also needed in the definition 'device for achieving power', so one word does two jobs.
annotationWithheld.clue: Brute gains device for achieving power

clue.text: Like Baby Jesus, was perhaps divine-led

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word was may be rearranged

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a divine, a clergyman
taken as written

explanation.surface: The infant Jesus, wrapped up, was guided by God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective in 'divine-led', but it is a noun, a theologian, abbreviated as a Doctor of Divinity; 'perhaps' scrambles 'was' to SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: Luke's gospel says the newborn Jesus was wrapped in swaddling clothes, so he was swaddled.

clue.text: Snail races got chaotic

indicators.note: chaotic suggests the letters of races got in disorder

explanation.surface: A snail race turns into a shambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French word for snail, used in English for a snail eaten as food.

clue.text: She's parted from man (name in 18), reportedly with ease

indicators.note: in means the name sits inside the letters standing for 18

parts.note: 18 across begins with Washington, and the US capital Washington is in DC, the District of Columbia
Ivor is a man's name

indicators.note: reportedly means the word ease is heard rather than read, sounding like a plural of the letter E

parts.note: spoken, ease sounds like Es, two of the letter E

explanation.surface: A woman has split from her husband, whose name is in the clue above, and finds it a relief.
explanation.walkthrough: '(name in 18)' looks like an aside naming the man; really 18 stands for WASHINGTON, so DC, with a name inside it. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorcee is a woman whose marriage has been legally ended, so she has parted from her husband.

clue.text: President with virgin material for man of letters from America

parts.note: George Washington was the first President of the United States

indicators.note: material suggests virgin is raw stuff to be reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: A President made use of untouched cloth to become an American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virgin material' reads as unused cloth, but 'material' is the anagram signal: VIRGIN rearranged gives IRVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington Irving, author of Rip Van Winkle, was an American writer, a man of letters.

clue.text: See 18
Short sailor needs sport and exercise

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
RU is rugby union, a sport
PT, physical training, is exercise

explanation.surface: A small seaman needs games and a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short sailor' reads as one phrase about a little seaman, but 'Short' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt means curt or brief, as in an abrupt answer, so it can mean short.

clue.text: Capital given to 19 to make music

definitions.meaning: added to 19 down's word it names a songwriter, the composer of White Christmas

explanation.walkthrough: 19 is IRVING; put this after it and you get Irving Berlin, the songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is Germany's capital, and Irving Berlin was the American composer of popular songs.

clue.text: 12's adversary, given to bore at length

definitions.meaning: the foe of Saint George in legend, the scaly beast he slew
to ... is to go on tediously for too long

explanation.walkthrough: 12 is GEORGE, England's patron saint, who killed the dragon in legend. 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George fought a dragon, and to drag on is to continue boringly, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Musical drama, "Alien Corn", can be made to work

parts.note: opera is drama set to music
blé is the French for corn, so foreign corn

explanation.surface: A show called Alien Corn turns out to be practical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien Corn' looks like the title of a play in quotes; 'Alien' just means foreign, so French corn, blé.
explanation.definitionFit: Something operable can be operated, made to function, so it can be made to work.

clue.text: What's left about, for example, like tatting …

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: tatting is a kind of handmade lace, so it is lacy
EG, exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: A remnant made of lace, like a scrap of tatting.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatting is a way of making lace by hand with a small shuttle, so tatting is lacy. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is what someone leaves you in their will, what's left to you.

clue.text: … and like what's left after disposal of 24s

definitions.text: and like what's left after disposal of 24s

parts.words: and like what's left after disposal of 24s
parts.note: follows on from the clue before; in a will, the estate remaining once the legacies have been paid out

explanation.walkthrough: 24 is LEGACY. In English law, the residuary estate is what is left after the specific legacies are paid out.
explanation.definitionFit: The residue of an estate is what remains after the legacies are paid, so it is residual.

clue.text: Thus I may not be the first person

definitions.text: Thus I may not be the first person

parts.words: Thus I may not be the first person
parts.note: a small i has a mark above it, while the capital I, the first person pronoun, does not

explanation.definitionFit: A lower-case letter i carries a dot, but the capital I that means me does not.

clue.text: Harold Wilson's seat once said to become more conspicuous

indicators.note: said means the place name is spoken and the sound gives the letters

parts.note: Huyton, near Liverpool, was the parliamentary seat of Prime Minister Harold Wilson

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister's constituency makes itself more prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson was a British Labour Prime Minister in the 1960s and 70s; his seat, Huyton near Liverpool, is pronounced much like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten is to increase or make stand out, so things that heighten become more noticeable.
